question: The formula unit mass of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a formula unit of a/an:
solution:
The correct answer is __**compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in its **formula unit**. For compounds, the formula unit represents the simplest ratio of the ions or atoms in the compound.
 
• This concept is applicable to both **ionic compounds** and **molecular compounds**. For example, the formula unit mass of sodium chloride (NaCl) is calculated by adding the atomic masses of sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl).
 
• In the case of a compound, the formula unit is representative of the smallest repeating unit that retains the compound’s chemical identity.
 
• The formula unit mass is expressed in **atomic mass units (amu)** or unified mass units (u), where 1 amu is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
